newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Rate cut buoys Australia stocks to new highs.
newsitem.headline: Rate cut buoys Australia stocks to new highs.

text.p: *Stocks open at record high buoyed by Friday's rate cut, with banks, insurers leading the way. Volume 73.56 million, value A$115.77 million, 547 stocks traded, 228 steady, 238 up, 81 down.

Australian stocks surged to yet another record high at the opening on Monday as sentiment remained buoyant after Friday's surprise interest rate cut by the Reserve Bank with banks and insurers leading the risers.

At 10.30 a.m. (0030 GMT), the All Ordinaries index was 9.1 points up at 2,573.0, but off a intra-day record high of 2,577.7 hit earlier. Brokers said volume was light with most of the action among interest rate sensitive stocks.
The June contract of the share price index was up seven points at 2565.0, but remained at a discount to the underlying physical market.

Despite the early surge, shares in market heavyweight BHP began to fall after it announced that trading conditions remained difficult and it expected a flat performance until it restructured and new projects came on stream.
"The highlights are the banks after the rate cut," said Gordon Furner a broker at ABN AMRO Hoare Govett.
Shares in Australia's largest bank, NAB hit a record high of A$19 earlier, but has since eased.
Insurance stocks were also stronger, with FAI topping the turnover with over 20 million shares traded. Brokers said the FAI trade was handled by Macquarie Equities.

The cut in offical cash rates by 0.5 percentage points to 5.5 percent by the RBA was seen as a boost for the housing market and consequently building material supplies, brokers said. The housing market is looking to consolidate a recovery.

The Australian building material index was the strongest riser but most indicies rose. Only the gold, telecommunications, alcohol and tobacco went against the positive trend. Shares in food wholesaler Davids Ltd were steady after the company announced a merger of its John Lewis unit with PFD Food Services to create Australia's largest food service company.

In other market news, Australian bond yields edged higher as the dust settled after Friday's rate cut. Turnover was fairly light, partly due to the holiday in the U.S. At 11.05 a.m. (0105 GMT), the 10-year T-bond was three points up at 7.60 percent.
The Australian dollar was finding its feet above US$0.7650, stablishing aftEr Friday'S heavy fall induced by thE rate cut, but there remained further near-term downside risks.
